chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and the group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad, from Kulayb ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The killer of Yahya ibn Zakariyya was conceived illegitimately, and the killer of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was also conceived illegitimately. The sky did not weep for anyone except for them.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, both, narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from his father, from al-Hasan, from Fudalah ibn Ayyub, from Kulayb ibn Mu'awiya al-Asadi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), similarly.

key_terms.يَحْيَى بْنِ زَكَرِيَّا: Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John son of Zechariah)

ai.seo_question: Who were the killers of Yahya and Husayn and what is their connection?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* draws a profound typological parallel between the martyrdom of Yahya ibn Zakariyya and Imam al-Husayn, identifying their respective killers as 'sons of illegitimacy' to signify a disruption of divine lineage and order. The statement that 'the sky wept only for them' underscores their unique cosmic status in Shia theology, marking their deaths as pivotal moments of heavenly grief distinct from other prophets. This connection reinforces the concept of *al-Walad al-Zina* as a marker of the enemies of truth, linking the Old Testament narrative to the pivotal event of Karbala.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father and all of my scholars narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, and from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Ja’far ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād, from Kulayb ibn Mu’āwiyah, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: The killer of Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (a.s.) was conceived illegitimately and the killer of Ḥusain (a.s.) (also) was conceived illegitimately. The sky has never cried on anyone but them.

The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan, and Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥusain, both from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from his father, from Ḥasan, from Faďālah ibn Ayyūb, from Kulayb ibn Mu’āwiyah Al-Asadi, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (a.s.).
